blocks.prompt: 1 (i) Find by definition, the derivatives w.r.t. '\(x\)' of the following functions defined as: \(2x^2 + 1\).
blocks.explanation:
Yeh sab se seedha qisam ka sawal hai: ek polynomial ka derivative, lekin definition se, yani limit ke zariye, rule se nahi.
Humein find karna hai \(f'(x)\) jab \(f(x) = 2x^2 + 1\).
Plan: chaar steps. Pehle \(x\) ki jagah \(x + \delta x\) rakhenge, phir purana \(f(x)\) minus karenge, phir \(\delta x\) se divide, aur aakhir mein \(\delta x \to 0\). Har step mein dekhte rehna ke \(\delta x\) kahan kahan aa raha hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = 2x^2 + 1\).
Find karna hai: \(f'(x)\), definition se.
Tareeqa: definition (first principles / ab-initio, yani bilkul shuru se) se derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). Chaar steps yaad rakhein: (I) \(f(x + \delta x)\) likhein; (II) us mein se \(f(x)\) minus karein; (III) \(\delta x\) se divide karein; (IV) \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein. Yeh tareeqa is liye ke Exercise 13.1 mein sawal khud 'by definition' maangta hai, aur power rule waghera abhi Section 13.6 mein aaenge; is liye shortcut nahi, poora limit ka safar dikhana hai.

Step I: \(f(x + \delta x)\) nikalein
\[f(x + \delta x) = 2(x + \delta x)^2 + 1\]
\[= 2\big(x^2 + 2x\,\delta x + (\delta x)^2\big) + 1\]
\[= 2x^2 + 4x\,\delta x + 2(\delta x)^2 + 1\]
Kyun: Function mein jahan jahan \(x\) hai, wahan \(x + \delta x\) rakhna hai, kyunke humein dekhna hai ke \(x\) thora sa badhne par function kitna badalta hai. Phir \((a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2\) se bracket kholte hain. Dhyan dein: \(2\) poore bracket ko multiply karta hai, sirf \(x^2\) ko nahi.

Step II: \(f(x)\) minus karein
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x)\]
\[= 2x^2 + 4x\,\delta x + 2(\delta x)^2 + 1 - 2x^2 - 1\]
\[= 4x\,\delta x + 2(\delta x)^2\]
Kyun: Yeh farq batata hai ke function kitna badla (change in \(y\), yani \(\delta y\)). \(2x^2\) aur \(1\) dono taraf hain, is liye cancel ho jate hain. Har sahi sawal mein is step ke baad har term mein kam az kam ek \(\delta x\) bachta hai; agar koi term bina \(\delta x\) ke bach jaye to samajh lein ghalti hui hai.

Step III: \(\delta x\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[= \dfrac{4x\,\delta x + 2(\delta x)^2}{\delta x}\]
\[= 4x + 2\,\delta x\]
Kyun: \(\delta x\) abhi sirf zero ki taraf ja raha hai, zero bana nahi, is liye us se divide karna jaiz hai. Isi cancel ki wajah se \(\frac{0}{0}\) wali mushkil khatam hoti hai.

Step IV: \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein
\[f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} (4x + 2\,\delta x)\]
\[= 4x + 2(0)\]
\[= 4x\]
Kyun: Ab \(\delta x\) kisi denominator mein nahi, is liye seedha \(\delta x = 0\) rakh sakte hain. \(2\,\delta x\) gaayab ho jata hai aur sirf \(4x\) bachta hai.

Tasdeeq: Section 13.6 ke power rule se (sirf jawab confirm karne ke liye, tareeqa nahi)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(2x^2 + 1) = 2(2x) + 0 = 4x \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Rule se bhi wohi jawab aaya, is liye hamara limit wala kaam sahi hai. Exam mein yeh check sirf rough par karein; jawab definition wala hi likhna hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (ii) Find by definition, the derivatives w.r.t. '\(x\)' of the following functions defined as: \(2 - \sqrt{x}\).
blocks.explanation:
Is sawal mein square root hai, aur square root wale sawal mein ek khaas trick lagti hai: rationalising (root ko upar se hatana).
Humein \(f'(x)\) chahiye jab \(f(x) = 2 - \sqrt{x}\).
Plan: chaar steps hi hain, lekin Step II ke baad upar \(\sqrt{x + \delta x} - \sqrt{x}\) aayega jis mein se \(\delta x\) bahar nahi nikalta. Is liye conjugate se multiply karke root hatayenge, phir \(\delta x\) cancel hoga.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = 2 - \sqrt{x}\), \(x > 0\).
Find karna hai: \(f'(x)\), definition se.
Tareeqa: definition (first principles / ab-initio, yani bilkul shuru se) se derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). Chaar steps yaad rakhein: (I) \(f(x + \delta x)\) likhein; (II) us mein se \(f(x)\) minus karein; (III) \(\delta x\) se divide karein; (IV) \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein. Yeh tareeqa is liye ke Exercise 13.1 mein sawal khud 'by definition' maangta hai, aur power rule waghera abhi Section 13.6 mein aaenge; is liye shortcut nahi, poora limit ka safar dikhana hai.

Step I aur II: \(f(x + \delta x)\) aur farq
\[f(x + \delta x) = 2 - \sqrt{x + \delta x}\]
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x)\]
\[= 2 - \sqrt{x + \delta x} - 2 + \sqrt{x}\]
\[= -\big(\sqrt{x + \delta x} - \sqrt{x}\big)\]
Kyun: \(x\) ki jagah \(x + \delta x\) rakha. Constant \(2\) dono mein hai, is liye cancel. Minus sign ko bahar nikal liya taake andar ek saaf \(\sqrt{x + \delta x} - \sqrt{x}\) reh jaye jo rationalise karna aasaan hai. Dhyan dein: \(-(-\sqrt{x}) = +\sqrt{x}\).

Upar wale hisse ko rationalise karein
\[\sqrt{x + \delta x} - \sqrt{x}\]
\[= \dfrac{(\sqrt{x + \delta x} - \sqrt{x})(\sqrt{x + \delta x} + \sqrt{x})}{\sqrt{x + \delta x} + \sqrt{x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{(x + \delta x) - x}{\sqrt{x + \delta x} + \sqrt{x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\delta x}{\sqrt{x + \delta x} + \sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: \((A - B)(A + B) = A^2 - B^2\) wala formula roots ko square kar ke khatam kar deta hai: \((\sqrt{x + \delta x})^2 = x + \delta x\). Upar aur neeche dono ko ek hi cheez se multiply kiya, is liye value nahi badli. Is ka faida yeh hai ke \(\delta x\) ab akela bahar aa gaya, jo agle step mein cancel hoga.

Step III: \(\delta x\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[= \dfrac{-\delta x}{\delta x\,(\sqrt{x + \delta x} + \sqrt{x})}\]
\[= \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{x + \delta x} + \sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: \(\delta x\) abhi zero nahi, sirf zero ke qareeb hai, is liye upar neeche se cancel karna bilkul jaiz hai. Minus sign upar hi rehta hai.

Step IV: limit lein
\[f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{x + \delta x} + \sqrt{x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{-1}{2\sqrt{x}}\]
Kyun: Ab neeche \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x} = 2\sqrt{x}\) banta hai jo zero nahi (\(x > 0\)), is liye seedha \(\delta x = 0\) rakhna theek hai.

Tasdeeq: Section 13.6 ke power rule se (sirf jawab confirm karne ke liye, tareeqa nahi)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\big(2 - x^{1/2}\big) = 0 - \tfrac{1}{2}x^{-1/2}\]
\[= \dfrac{-1}{2\sqrt{x}} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\sqrt{x}\) ko \(x^{1/2}\) likh kar power rule lagaya to wohi jawab aaya. Matlab rationalising wala kaam sahi tha.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iii) Find by definition, the derivatives w.r.t. '\(x\)' of the following functions defined as: \(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\).
blocks.explanation:
Yahan do mushkilen ikatthi hain: fraction bhi hai aur square root bhi.
Humein \(f'(x)\) chahiye jab \(f(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\).
Plan: pehle do fractions ko common denominator (saanjha neeche wala) bana kar ek fraction banayenge, phir upar wale roots ko conjugate se rationalise karenge, phir \(\delta x\) cancel, aur aakhir mein limit. Thora lamba hai, lekin har qadam choti si baat hai.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\), \(x > 0\).
Find karna hai: \(f'(x)\), definition se.
Tareeqa: definition (first principles / ab-initio, yani bilkul shuru se) se derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). Chaar steps yaad rakhein: (I) \(f(x + \delta x)\) likhein; (II) us mein se \(f(x)\) minus karein; (III) \(\delta x\) se divide karein; (IV) \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein. Yeh tareeqa is liye ke Exercise 13.1 mein sawal khud 'by definition' maangta hai, aur power rule waghera abhi Section 13.6 mein aaenge; is liye shortcut nahi, poora limit ka safar dikhana hai.

Step I aur II: ek fraction banayein
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x)\]
\[= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x + \delta x}} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{x}}\]
\[= \dfrac{\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x + \delta x}}{\sqrt{x}\,\sqrt{x + \delta x}}\]
Kyun: Do fractions minus karne ke liye neeche ek jaisa hona chahiye. Common denominator \(\sqrt{x}\,\sqrt{x + \delta x}\) liya: pehle fraction ko upar neeche \(\sqrt{x}\) se aur doosre ko \(\sqrt{x + \delta x}\) se multiply kiya. Dhyan dein ke upar order \(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x + \delta x}\) hai, ulta nahi.

Upar ko rationalise karein
\[(\sqrt{x} - \sqrt{x + \delta x})(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x + \delta x})\]
\[= x - (x + \delta x)\]
\[= -\delta x\]
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x) = \dfrac{-\delta x}{\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x + \delta x}\,(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x + \delta x})}\]
Kyun: Upar aur neeche dono ko conjugate \(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x + \delta x}\) se multiply kiya. Upar \(A^2 - B^2\) ban kar roots khatam ho gaye aur \(-\delta x\) bacha. Neeche ko hum factor form mein hi rehne dete hain, kyunke aakhir mein wahan sirf \(\delta x = 0\) rakhna hai; usay kholna waqt ka zaya hai.

Step III: \(\delta x\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[= \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{x}\sqrt{x + \delta x}\,(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x + \delta x})}\]
Kyun: Upar wala \(\delta x\) aur jis \(\delta x\) se divide kiya, dono cancel. Yeh tab hi ho saka jab rationalise kar ke \(\delta x\) ko root se azaad kiya.

Step IV: limit lein
\[f'(x) = \dfrac{-1}{\sqrt{x}\,\sqrt{x}\,(\sqrt{x} + \sqrt{x})}\]
\[= \dfrac{-1}{x \cdot 2\sqrt{x}}\]
\[= -\dfrac{1}{2x^{3/2}} = -\dfrac{1}{2}x^{-3/2}\]
Kyun: \(\delta x = 0\) rakha to har \(\sqrt{x + \delta x}\) ban gaya \(\sqrt{x}\). Phir \(\sqrt{x}\cdot\sqrt{x} = x\), aur \(x \cdot \sqrt{x} = x^{1} \cdot x^{1/2} = x^{3/2}\) (powers add hoti hain). Answer key \(-\frac{1}{2}x^{-3/2}\) likhti hai, jo isi ka doosra roop hai.

Tasdeeq: Section 13.6 ke power rule se (sirf jawab confirm karne ke liye, tareeqa nahi)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\,x^{-1/2} = -\tfrac{1}{2}x^{-3/2} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{x}} = x^{-1/2}\). Power rule mein nayi power \(-\frac{1}{2} - 1 = -\frac{3}{2}\) banti hai. Wohi jawab, to kaam sahi hai.

blocks.prompt: 1 (iv) Find by definition, the derivatives w.r.t. '\(x\)' of the following functions defined as: \(x(x - 3)\).
blocks.explanation:
Dekhne mein yeh do cheezon ka product lagta hai, lekin bracket kholein to seedha polynomial ban jata hai.
Humein \(f'(x)\) chahiye jab \(f(x) = x(x - 3)\).
Plan: pehle \(x(x - 3) = x^2 - 3x\) kar lenge, kyunke polynomial ke saath chaar steps bohat saaf chalte hain. Phir wohi chaar steps.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(f(x) = x(x - 3) = x^2 - 3x\).
Find karna hai: \(f'(x)\), definition se.
Tareeqa: definition (first principles / ab-initio, yani bilkul shuru se) se derivative: \(f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} \frac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\). Chaar steps yaad rakhein: (I) \(f(x + \delta x)\) likhein; (II) us mein se \(f(x)\) minus karein; (III) \(\delta x\) se divide karein; (IV) \(\delta x \to 0\) ka limit lein. Yeh tareeqa is liye ke Exercise 13.1 mein sawal khud 'by definition' maangta hai, aur power rule waghera abhi Section 13.6 mein aaenge; is liye shortcut nahi, poora limit ka safar dikhana hai.

Step I: \(f(x + \delta x)\) nikalein
\[f(x + \delta x) = (x + \delta x)^2 - 3(x + \delta x)\]
\[= x^2 + 2x\,\delta x + (\delta x)^2 - 3x - 3\,\delta x\]
Kyun: Har \(x\) ki jagah \(x + \delta x\). \((x + \delta x)^2\) ko formula se khola aur \(-3\) ko bracket ke dono terms se multiply kiya. Dhyan dein: \(-3\) sirf \(x\) ko nahi, \(\delta x\) ko bhi multiply karta hai.

Step II: \(f(x)\) minus karein
\[f(x + \delta x) - f(x)\]
\[= 2x\,\delta x + (\delta x)^2 - 3\,\delta x\]
Kyun: \(f(x) = x^2 - 3x\) minus kiya to \(x^2\) aur \(-3x\) dono cancel ho gaye. Bachi hui har term mein \(\delta x\) hai, jo ishara hai ke ab tak sab theek hai.

Step III: \(\delta x\) se divide karein
\[\dfrac{f(x + \delta x) - f(x)}{\delta x}\]
\[= 2x + \delta x - 3\]
Kyun: Har term se ek \(\delta x\) cancel hua. \(\delta x\) abhi zero nahi, is liye divide karna jaiz hai.

Step IV: limit lein
\[f'(x) = \lim_{\delta x \to 0} (2x + \delta x - 3)\]
\[= 2x - 3\]
Kyun: Ab koi denominator nahi, seedha \(\delta x = 0\) rakh diya; beech wala \(\delta x\) gaayab ho gaya.

Tasdeeq: Section 13.6 ke power rule se (sirf jawab confirm karne ke liye, tareeqa nahi)
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}(x^2 - 3x) = 2x - 3 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Rule se bhi wohi jawab, is liye hamara kaam sahi hai.
